thread:
Alex: Quick question — seeing a couple of customers report billed tokens way higher than they expect when they use streaming + max_tokens. Repro looks like prompt truncation is shifting tokens into the completion side. Anyone seen this?

smiller: Hmm, repro steps?

Alex: Minimal repro: long prompt (~10k tokens), request with max_tokens=512, enable_stream=true. Runtime truncates the prompt to model.max_seq, then we stream partials. Billing records show completion_tokens inflated vs what we expect. Request body:

```json
{"model":"gpt-xxl","prompt":"<huge prompt>","max_tokens":512,"stream":true}
```

Sasha: I think this is the cached-prefix + streaming interaction. Our accounting currently attributes tokens based on the concatenated final buffer used for decoding, not the original user prompt. If truncation happens earlier in the pipeline we lose the original prompt length and end up attributing tokens as completion.

owen: Proposal: expose both the original and the counted token counts. Keep existing "prompt_tokens"/"completion_tokens" semantics (what billing uses) but add: "prompt_tokens_original", "prompt_tokens_counted_after_truncation", and "prompt_truncation_reason" (values: "max_seq", "user_truncate", "none"). Also include cached variants: "cached_prompt_tokens" and "cached_completion_tokens" with origin hints.

billing-bot: Heads up — we cannot change billed fields without a migration plan. Any added fields must be opt-in and we should default to current values for backward compat. Notify customers if their dashboards will show new numbers. :warning:

Alex: Agreed. My goal is clarity for debugging and reconciliations, not to change billing. So new fields should be read-only, non-billable reporting fields. Something like:

```json
{"prompt_tokens": 2048, "completion_tokens": 512, "prompt_tokens_original": 10240, "prompt_tokens_after_truncation": 2048, "prompt_truncation_reason": "max_seq", "cached_prompt_tokens": 512}
```

Sasha: +1 for that shape. We should also surface a boolean "streaming_truncation_edgecase" so infra + billing can filter out these events during recon.

owen: Implementation notes: accounting happens in two places (pre-decoder attribution and post-decoder finalization). We can capture original prompt length at request parse time and stash into the request context. If model truncates internally, we already have the parse-time value. Then finalization can populate the new fields without touching the canonical "prompt_tokens" (billing) field. Should be low-risk.

infra-lead: Sounds reasonable. Please create a short spec PR describing field names, types (ints/strings), and migration notes. I'll link to RW-4012 and assign to eng-platform. We need a doc blurb for the billing team and a comms plan for customers who rely on token breakdowns.

Alex: I'll open the spec tonight. Quick questions for the PR reviewers: preferred field names (snake_case vs camelCase) and where to put them in streaming payload (top-level meta vs per-chunk headers). My vote: snake_case top-level fields in the final response JSON and headers for quick ingest.

smiller: prefer snake_case for parity with existing token fields. Top-level makes debugging easier. headers are nice but fragmented.

Sasha: Agreed. Top-level final response fields + optional header hints (x-rw-prompt-original-tokens) for streaming consumers.

billing-bot: Also add a flag we can toggle server-side to opt into the new reporting for a subset of customers so we can compare numbers before a full rollout.

Alex: Good call. I'll add an "opt_in_reporting" config in the spec and a small experimental rollout plan. Will ping infra + billing when PR is ready.

infra-lead: I'll triage RW-4012 and schedule a short async review window tomorrow afternoon. Thanks for surfacing this.

Sasha: I'll draft the docs PR (#542) and include examples for recon teams.

smiller: Ack. :+1:

Alex: Thanks all — will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
